AGENDA
  GLENDALE BLUE RIBBON PENSION REVIEW COMMITTEE
  VIA TELECONFERENCE ONLY
 Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
 verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
 glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices
 using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings are also
 archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818) 548-4013 for
 program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk's Office.
 If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the
 Management Services Department at (818) 548-4844, during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM
 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  OCTOBER 4, 2021 AT 6:30 PM

To help slow the transmission of COVID-19, and protect the health and safety of the community, City
Council, as well as Board & Commission meetings, will continue to be closed to the public for in-person
attendance.
The public is encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social
distancing. Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and
AT&T U-verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices
using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu.
For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a
specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed.

  a. Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the October 4, 2021
  Special Meeting of the Blue Ribbon Pension Review Committee was Posted on
  October 1, 2021, on the Bulletin Board Outside City Hall.
2. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items NOT a part of this agenda. Committee may question or
  respond to the speaker but there will be no debate or decision. Staff may refer the
  matter to the appropriate department for investigation and report.

4. BUSINESS ITEMS

minutes_text:
CITY OF GLENDALE
  BLUE RIBBON PENSION REVIEW COMMITTEE
  REGULAR MEETING MINUTES

  October 4, 2021

ROLL CALL

Meeting began at 6:36pm

Present: Finch, Manning, Masias, Michals, Palos, Bain, Wenz, Kedikian, Amirian,
Knights, Molano, Wolfson

Absent: Nelson, Zakarain, IBEW rep

Staff: Doyle, Takhtalian, Flynn, Garcia, Hovsepian, Bradford, Cerritos, Jensen,
Holtzman, Soghomonyan

  1. REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA
  a. Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. Mr. Soghomonyan reported
  that The Agenda for the October 4, 2021 Special Meeting of the Blue
  Ribbon Pension Review Committee was Posted on October 1, 2021, on
  the Bulletin Board Outside City Hall.

  2. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None

  3. MINUTES
  None

  4. BUSINESS ITEMS

  a. Rules of Order and Procedures
  i. Ratify Rules of Order and Procedures

Holtzman moved to ratify Rules of Order and Procedures. Manning requests that
section 2.3 be renumbered to section 2.2. Molano requests that executive summaries
be given before presentations are given to committee. Molano requests that agenda be
sent electronically upon request by members of the public. Holtzman agrees with
Manning that section 2.3 should be re-numbered 2.2. Holtzman agrees with Molano that
the rules should allow for agendas to be emailed or mailed. Holtzman notes that some
documents will be suited to have executive summaries, and some will not. Wolfson
requests that section 4.1 shall read as “a list shall be kept of all proposed agenda items
to be incorporated in minutes of the meetings.” Wolfson requests that there be time limit

  1
 on presentations. Holtzman clarifies that agenda items proposed in executive committee
meetings will be kept in executive committee minutes and that such minutes will be
available to the public. Holtzman does not think that there should be a time limit on
presentations.

Amirian motions to amend the Rules of Order and Procedures with the following
changes: renumber section 2.3 to 2.2, add that agenda can be sent electronically upon
request by members of the public.
Bain seconds

Aye: Amirian, Bain, Kedikian, Knights, Manning, Masias, Michals, Molano, Wolfson,
Finch, Wenz, Palos
Noes: none

Motion passes

Molano motions to add that presentations to the Committee will be prefaced by an oral
summary of up to 2-3 minutes
Seconded by Wolfson

Ayes: Molano, Wolfson
Noes: Amirian, Bain, Kedikian, Knights, Manning, Masias, Michals, Finch, Wentz

Motion fails

Holtzman asks for public comment. There is no public comment.

Amirian motions to ratify Rules of Order and Procedures as amended.
Manning seconds

Ayes: Amirian, Bain, Kedekian, Knights, Manning, Masias, Michals, Molano, Wolfson,
Finch, Wenz, Palos
Noes: none

Motion passes

  b. Selection of Executive Committee
Holtzman discusses the purpose of the Executive Committee, noting that the goal is to
get a broad cross section of perspectives on the Executive Committee. Holtzman
proposes that individuals volunteer for the Executive Committee; if more than 5
volunteer, then Committee will vote on the volunteers and those with the highest
plurality will be chosen for the Executive Committee.

  2
 Amirian asks if members can nominate other members. Holtzman answers that
members can nominate other members.

Amirian nominates Manning
Manning declines nomination due to time constraints
Amirian nominates Bain
Seconded by Wolfson
Wolfson nominates Molano
Seconded by Masias
Kedikian nominates Amirian
Seconded by Molano
Wenz nominates Finch
Seconded by Amirian
Molano nominates Michals
Seconded by Amirian
Michals accepts, nomination but notes a concern about the time commitment.

Manning motions that Executive Committee will be composed of: Bain, Molano, Amirian,
Finch and Michals
Wolfson Seconds

Ayes: Amirian, Bain, Kedikian, Knights, Manning, Masias, Michals, Molano, Wolfson,
Finch, Wenz, Palos
Noes: none

Motion passes
  c. Background on Glendale’s Pension Obligations – Presentation and Q&A
Holtzman introduces presentation and requests that members hold questions until the
end.
Presentation given by Takhtalian and Flynn regarding:
   Definitions
   PERS historical background
   Pre and post PEPRE benefit formulas available to public agencies
   How PERA retirement benefits are calculated
   Pension reform in Glendale
   Hypothetical PERS Termination
   Implications of Terminating Pension Plan
   Financial Data

Wolfson asks: what is proportion of current workforce who are PEPRA employees vs.
classic employees? Wolfson asks: does City currently offer employees option of
deferred compensation in 457 plan? Wolfson asks: Can all agencies who are members
apply pressure to CalPERS regarding reduced computations? Wolfson notes that during

  3
 2015-16 the City’s obligation was about $460 million and now it is $640 million. Wolfson
asks what is the impact of PEPRA?

Flynn answers: for the miscellaneous plan, as of last year, 42% of the workforce is in
PEPRA. In Safety it is 19%, which is a function of longevity in safety as opposed to
miscellaneous. Employees can join a 457 plan, and there is no employer match on that.
Flynn also notes that in FY 31-32 the consultant projects that the City’s rate will drop as
a result of more of the workforce becoming PEPRA employees.

Holtzman comments that UAL generated is a dollar number and that the City is paying
interest on that amount at the discount rate. He notes that unless CalPERS makes its
returns of 7% or better, then the City is actually losing ground. So the problem is that
cities have a giant sum of money that is owed and isn’t going away quickly.

Molano asks: what does it mean that CalPERS took the rosiest indicators of stock
market and applied them as if it were going to last forever? He comments that the City
needs to see CalPERS as the agency who it depends on to make returns because
otherwise the tax payers pick up that cost. Molano states that the Committee should
reframe CalPERS costs in terms of their impact on the quality of life of residents. Bain
comments that underneath UAL is the accrued liability; when CalPERS cuts the interest
rate by .5%, they are in effect raising the accrued liability by over .5%, so the increases
are tied to interest assumption changes.
Holtzman comments that this creates a conundrum: lowering the discount rate
increases the accrued liability.Bain notes that it is better to have the two in alignment.

  5. REPORTS
  a. Reports of Sub-committees and Committee Members

  Skipped.

  b. Brown Act Training by City Attorney

  Skipped.

  6. REQUESTS FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS
  None

  7. ADJOURNMENT

Manning motions to adjourn
Amirian seconds

Ayes: Amirian, Bain, Kedikian, Knights, Manning, Masias, Michals, Molano, Wolfson,
Finch, Wenz, Palos

  4
 Motion passes and meeting adjourns at 8:34pm.
